blocker.summary: r437-r439 established via three independent methods (live watchpoint spanning the full run, Ghidra reference search, exhaustive text search of all 77 generated translation units) that the null global pointer at guest address 0x82935D98 that sub_821D6C20 crashes on is never written anywhere in the reachable compiled code -- and corrected a methodology mistake along the way (r437 had queried the wrong-SHA Ghidra project; the correct one is ac6-us). r440 wrote a new, narrowly-scoped, correctly SHA-gated tool (scripts/DecompileD6C20Dispatcher.java, committed) to disassemble+decompile just sub_821D6C20 and its caller sub_821D7DE0 in the correct ac6-us project (run without -readOnly since the project directory is gitignored/local/reversible; two functions only, not a full-binary reseed). The decompiled output is substantive: sub_821D7DE0 is the game's main loop entry -- it calls sub_821D5F48 then sub_821D6C20 as two 'must succeed' initialization steps (identical assert-fail-on-zero pattern for both) immediately before an infinite do-while game loop. sub_821D6C20 dereferences *0x82935D98 completely unguarded as its literal first action (the crash site) -- consistent with retail code expecting the object to already be constructed by this point, not defensively checked here. The rest of its body (success branch) reads ~35 indexed settings values and pushes each into that object's vtable (and a few related objects) at specific offsets, ending with capability-flag calls -- a textbook 'configure a rendering/GPU device from title settings' shape, not a generic dispatcher. Strong new hypothesis: *0x82935D98 is the game's renderer/GPU device manager, never constructed in this offline environment -- plausibly the same underlying gap already named by r425 (VdSwap never carries a real PresentPacket) and r434/r435 (real visual content never wired). Not yet confirmed (would need decompiling sub_821D5F48 and the settings-reading helper functions, named for r441) and still no writer found in reachable code -- committing native_vulkan_backend.cpp's backlog (r433/r434/r438) remains the other open, user-dependent thread.
